title.narrative: SALAR: Support to Public Administration Reform in Moldova 2025-2028
SALAR: Support to Public Administration Reform in Moldova 2025-2028

description.narrative: In 2024 it was agreed to support an Inception phase and to work more thoroughly on the concept of support that would cover local and central administration reform as well as EU integration agenda. The overall objective of the project is: Strengthened local public administration within an enhanced framework for local governance improve service provision to citizens in line with the country’s strategic orientation towards EU accession.

År 2024 enades man om att stödja en inledningsfas och att arbeta mer grundligt med konceptet stöd som skulle omfatta reformer av lokal och central förvaltning samt EU:s integrationsagenda. Projektets övergripande mål är: Stärkt lokal offentlig förvaltning inom ett förbättrat ramverk för lokalt styre och förbättrad service till medborgarna i linje med landets strategiska inriktning mot EU-medlemskap.

Overall objective (impact): Strengthened LPAs within an enhanced framework for local governance improve service provision to citizens in line with the countrys strategic orientation towards EU accession.
Component 1: Coordination of local governance Outcome: Improved central coordination of local governance in relation to distribution of functions, local PAR, service delivery, and inter-ministerial coordination.
Component 2: Service delivery in selected LPAs Outcome: Selected clusters of LPAs improve joint provision of public services in line with strategic priorities defined together with citizens.
Component 3: Local engagement in EU integration Outcome: LPA engagement in the EU accession process strengthened and local access to EU funds facilitated.

2025 In relation to Outcome 1: Improved central coordination of local governance in relation to distribution of functions, local PAR, service delivery, and inter-ministerial coordination, State Chancellery (SC) reform team was supported in advancing local public administration reform priorities. Project contributed to central coordination capacities by financing expert positions within the SC reform team, including support for reform planning, digitalisation and data-driven performance monitoring of local public authorities (LPAs). Facilitated community consultations on voluntary amalgamation, engaging mayors, councillors and citizens and contributing evidence and recommendations to the SCs implementation of Law No. 225/2023. The project advanced preparations for improving local digital services by supporting governance arrangements around the e-APL platform and developing data performance tools to strengthen evidence-based decision-making by LPAs. Progress on clarifying the division of functions between different levels of government was limited, as the SC prioritised voluntary amalgamation and reform implementation over functional mapping during the reporting period.
In relation to Outcome 2: Selected clusters of LPAs improve joint provision of public services in line with strategic priorities defined together with citizens It was completed the first round of cluster selection, identifying two amalgamating LPA clusters for support packages and establishing a pipeline for an additional selection round in 2026. It were conducted extensive consultations and field assessments with potential clusters, enabling LPAs to define investment priorities through participatory processes and identify concrete service delivery and infrastructure needs. It was also developed a portfolio of potential investments, technical documentation and feasibility support aimed at improving service delivery and facilitating larger infrastructure investments in amalgamating communities. It were established partnerships and dialogue with Swedish municipalities to support future knowledge exchange on citizen service delivery and local digital solutions.
Referring to Outcome 3: LPA engagement in the EU accession process strengthened and local access to EU funds facilitated In the reporting period it was successfully launched the EU Local Ambassadors Network, creating a platform that brings together mayors, technical staff, CALM and national stakeholders to strengthen local participation in the EU accession process. It were organised 15 nationwide information sessions reaching more than 480 local officials from 35 districts, increasing awareness of EU accession, available funding opportunities and the role of LPAs in implementing EU-related reforms. It was also supported dialogue on mechanisms to improve local access to EU financing, including promoting the Montenegro Revolving Fund model and engaging national decision-makers on its potential application in Moldova.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
